prompt: Design the temporal model and conversion/update policy for this system.

Refresh or invalidate dependent reminders as well as the cached UTC value
The preserved local value avoids requiring old rules to reconstruct it

Old rules are necessary even though the source local value is retained
This synthetic policy change happened in a real jurisdiction

prompt: Design the temporal model and conversion/update policy for this system.
context: A synthetic local-to-instant mapper returns zero candidates for appointment A and two for B. Both appointments promise a selected local date/time in a named zone. The current application blindly takes the first candidate, or shifts the value if none exists, without a documented product policy. A tzdb update can also make a previously unique appointment ambiguous. No real-world transition dates are implied.
required_findings: Define an explicit product policy for both missing and ambiguous local times
Re-evaluate affected records when rules change, not only at initial entry
Do not silently choose an occurrence or shift the appointment without an agreed policy
forbidden_findings: Every local date/time maps to exactly one instant
Lenient conversion is universally correct
Reject all ambiguous times as the only valid product policy
Claim tests passed without execution evidence

prompt: Design the temporal model and conversion/update policy for this system.
context: A team meets every Monday at 09:00 in the organizer-selected named zone, with participants in other zones. The first occurrence is stored in UTC; all following occurrences are produced by adding exactly 168 hours. The coordinating zone changes offset during the series and participants may change offsets on different dates.
required_findings: Retain the recurrence rule and coordinating zone
Resolve individual occurrences and attendee views with their applicable rules
Adding 168 elapsed hours is not sufficient to preserve this local-time recurrence
forbidden_findings: A single fixed UTC offset covers the whole recurring series
The recurrence must be anchored to each attendee zone simultaneously

prompt: Review whether this stored appointment supports future time-zone rule changes.
context: A venue appointment stores 2032-06-15T09:00+02:00. The venue is expected to keep the appointment at local 09:00 even if its rules change. No named zone or venue location is retained.
required_findings: A numeric offset does not identify the zone whose future rules apply
The local component remains available if the storage type preserves it, but a zone or source location is missing
Verify storage semantics instead of assuming the database preserves the supplied offset
forbidden_findings: The numeric offset is a time-zone identity
Every database offset timestamp retains the original offset
Discard the local component and store only UTC

prompt: Design the appointment time model for this venue booking system.
context: The appointment must occur at 09:00 at its physical venue. The address is authoritative; its location-to-zone assignment may change before the event. A cached zone ID is currently determined at booking time. No geographic service is selected.
required_findings: Preserve the venue location and source local date/time
Treat the location-to-zone assignment as potentially derived and reviewable
Recompute dependent conversions if the applicable zone changes without prescribing an unspecified service
forbidden_findings: Zone identity can never change for a venue
Require a geographic service for every timestamp in every application

context: A device supplied yesterday's local date/time and named zone. The importer used a stale rules database, stored only the computed UTC value, and discarded the source input and conversion provenance. Correct conversion is important, but no trustworthy original instant was supplied.
required_findings: Recent-past conversion can be incorrect when the rules used were stale
Discarding source input impairs later correction
Do not invent a corrected instant or claim certainty without the missing source/provenance
forbidden_findings: Past values are necessarily correct
A directly observed instant and a UTC value converted from local input have identical provenance
Reconstruct the original local value reliably using only the newest rules
